To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Japanese state is a weak state, and that the Japanese people are a weak people.
the Fukushima disaster is not over, that the nuclear industry is not safe, and that we are not safe.
the nuclear meltdown is an unprecedented event, that there is no way to know how much radiation is leaking from the reactors, and that there is no safe level of radiation exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do you make a profit out of the uncertainty of the nuclear future

the following questions: What does the Fukushima nuclear disaster reveal about the relationship between the nuclear industry, the global financial industry, the state, and the public? How does this relationship shape the way we imagine the future of energy? How does the nuclear disaster affect the future of energy in the global South? What are the political implications of the Fukushima nuclear disaster?

the following questions: How can the uncertainty of the long-term consequences of low-level radiation be managed and capitalized? How does the nuclear disaster produce a “necropolitical” condition of life and death that is not only about life and death, but about life and death in relation to the production of value? What are the implications of the nuclear disaster for the future of capitalism?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nuclear catastrophe in Japan is a laboratory of necropolitics, a site of the production of the dead as a new form of capital, and that it is the responsibility of the living to prevent the further production of the dead.

the nuclear disaster in Fukushima has become the most important laboratory for the development and implementation of a new type of global governance, a governance that is based on the assumption that the human body is a site of economic and necropolitical experimentation, and that the human body can be treated like a financial instrument.
the nuclear disaster has created the conditions for a new kind of global financial and necropolitics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is a study in the ways that the nuclear accident in Japan has been a laboratory for the development of new forms of necropolitical and financial governance.

we seek to understand the ways in which the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster has become an object of speculative financial calculation, and to understand the implications of this for the future of the nuclear regime.
the Fukushima disaster was a laboratory for the development of a necrocapitalist regime of low-level radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fukushima nuclear disaster is not a “natural disaster,” but a “man-made disaster,” which can be understood in terms of a “necropolitics” of nuclear energy.
